court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Subordinate Judge, Harur, Dharmapuri District (H.M.O.P. No.55 of 2025)
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized on 13.04.2022. They have no children and due to matrimonial disputes, they started living separately. The respondent filed H.M.O.P. No.55 of 2025 seeking divorce under Section 13(1)(ia) and 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The convenience of the parties is a relevant consideration in determining whether to transfer a case.
legal_principles.held: Having considered the above circumstances, and bearing in mind the convenience of the parties, this Court is satisfied that the transfer sought deserves to be ordered.

legal_principles.principle: A court may order the transfer of a case to avoid multiplicity and inconvenience.
legal_principles.held: it would be appropriate that the matrimonial proceedings between the parties are tried within the same jurisdiction to avoid multiplicity and inconvenience

outcome.final_order: Transfer sought deserves to be ordered. The matrimonial proceedings between the parties are tried within the same jurisdiction to avoid multiplicity and inconvenience.

use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition for divorce case
advising on jurisdiction in family law matters
preparing a withdrawal application in a matrimonial dispute
